rig.key_off_stations: fill_scale 0: no front light at all, only a source behind the actor -- near-silhouette with a rim

catchlight_pass.model: a mirror sphere of the measured corneal radius at each eye, from relight/eye_geometry.json, rendered with the PLATE camera
catchlight_pass.reflectance: dielectric Fresnel, ~2.5% at normal incidence. A 100% mirror returned the whole cornea at 2.5-4.3 linear and would have whited out both eyes
catchlight_pass.visible_to_camera: the corneal spheres ONLY. The proxy stays in the scene as an occluder -- brow, nose and cheek block part of the environment from reaching the cornea -- but is hidden from camera rays, as are the bulb and the fill, so this pass is purely additive
catchlight_pass.why_no_threshold: presence, size, shape, colour and occlusion all come from the scene. A mirror shows the source RADIANCE, which does not fall off with distance, so a distant lamp still makes a catchlight -- a small one. A distance rule would get sunlight backwards

note: Clay-skin proxy only: no plate texture, so every value on screen is computed geometry and light rather than photography.
